extra.message: The JWT signing secret (jwt.base64-secret) is a hardcoded, publicly-known value committed to source control and used as-is in the production profile. This value is bound via SecurityProperties.base64Secret (eladmin-system/src/main/java/me/zhengjie/modules/security/config/SecurityProperties.java:46) and used by TokenProvider to sign/verify all JWTs. Anyone with read access to this (open-source) repository knows the exact signing key used by any deployment that does not override it, allowing them to forge arbitrary JWTs (including admin tokens) and fully bypass authentication.

extra.message: Same hardcoded JWT base64-secret as application-prod.yml is duplicated in the dev profile and consumed by SecurityProperties/TokenProvider for signing all session JWTs. A static, source-controlled secret lets anyone forge valid authentication tokens for any user/role.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: A full RSA private key (rsa.private_key) is hardcoded in the shared application.yml. It is loaded by RsaProperties (eladmin-common/src/main/java/me/zhengjie/config/properties/RsaProperties.java:34-36) and used in AuthController.java:82 and UserController.java:158-159,189 to decrypt the user's login password and password-change payloads. Since this key is public (checked into source), anyone can decrypt any password encrypted with the matching public key in transit for any deployment that keeps the default configuration, completely defeating the password-encryption-in-transit scheme.

extra.message: The global CorsFilter bean sets config.setAllowCredentials(true) together with config.addAllowedOriginPattern("*"), registered for every path ("/**"). This allows any origin on the internet to make credentialed cross-site requests (cookies/Authorization headers sent) against the API, enabling cross-site request forgery / credential theft against authenticated endpoints from an attacker-controlled page.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The Druid SQL monitoring console (stat-view-servlet) is enabled at /druid/* in the production profile with a hardcoded, well-known default login-username: admin / login-password: 123456, and no IP allow-list restricting access (`allow:` is empty). An attacker who reaches the production host can log into the Druid console with these default credentials and view live SQL statements, connection pool stats, session attributes and web request parameters, leaking sensitive data and database connection details.

The production datasource password falls back to a hardcoded default (${DB_PWD:123456}) when the DB_PWD environment variable is not set, so a deployment that forgets to configure the env var silently runs with a well-known weak credential against the database.

GET /api/serverDeploy returns ServerDeployDto objects (eladmin-system/src/main/java/me/zhengjie/modules/maint/service/dto/ServerDeployDto.java:48-49) that include the raw SSH `password` field with no masking/redaction. The password is also persisted in plaintext on the ServerDeploy entity (eladmin-system/src/main/java/me/zhengjie/modules/maint/domain/ServerDeploy.java:48-49) with no encryption annotation. Any user holding the 'serverDeploy:list' permission receives the cleartext SSH credentials for every registered deployment server in the API response.
